coaching.headline: Every neutral objective was ours, four kills conceded all game, and Serath went eight for zero. That was a proper fucking beating.
coaching.team: The team took every river buff, all three Seedlings, the Mini Prime and the only Fangtooth, took three outer towers to one and gave up four kills. Serath and Lt. Belica never died. The one lost fight went 1-3, with Lt. Belica's kill on Gadget the team's only kill there, and the team still took an enemy outer tower and the Mini Prime afterward. The first two clean fights, including a four-for-zero, were followed by no structure; whether a tower was reachable then is unknown.

focus.title: Clean fight, then a tower
focus.action: After a fight with kills for the team and no allied deaths, the team calls the nearest enemy tower and hits the tower together once an allied minion wave arrives, before any player splits off. Kills without a structure are a lap dance with no finish.

13.5.call: Lt. Belica killed Gadget, then Sparrow killed TwinBlast and Steel, and Skylar finished Renna. Sparrow was the enemy's top hero damage dealer. With Gadget down and Sparrow standing, the next stun goes on Sparrow or we back off together.

16.7.call: Steel opened by killing Sparrow, Serath dropped Narbash and Lt. Belica finished Skylar, nobody lost, and the Fangtooth was ours in that window. Two more enemy outer towers fell before the end, against one of ours. That is the template.

20.7.call: Serath killed Scarlett and Sparrow, the last two kills of the game, in the same window as the third enemy outer tower falling, and the game ended shortly after. With the enemy jungler and carry dead, the whole team pushes together.

16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Goldilocks324 ran a proper tank-support game: the most wards placed in the game, a hand in nearly half our kills, the second-most damage mitigated on our team and one death. Steady as a brick shithouse.

Sparrow killed TwinBlast and Steel in the one fight the team lost. Force Shield blocks enemy projectiles, so when Sparrow starts shooting at TwinBlast, Steel drops the wall between Sparrow and TwinBlast before stepping in with Shield Bash.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Mr_Meat31 put up the third-highest hero damage in the game on TwinBlast, just behind Serath, died once and cleared both enemy wards the team destroyed. Solid shit from the carry seat.

TwinBlast and Steel both fell to Sparrow in the lost fight. Heightened Senses gives Sparrow stealth, movement speed and attack speed, so TwinBlast holds Rocket Dash until Sparrow reappears and steps out before trading back.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Willy Guggenheim ran the best damage game in the lobby: the most hero damage of anyone, zero deaths, farm well above the recorded Belica norm and Gadget dead to Lt. Belica twice. Gadget, favored on paper, finished without a kill.
Zero deaths at the top of the damage chart is the bar now. Gadget's Security Gate roots, so Lt. Belica waits for the gate to be spent before closing in for Seismic Assault.
1e79d5d8-b822-4f1f-8e33-c946cef2e950: Serath ran this fucking game: eight kills, zero deaths, by far the most objective damage and the most healing in the game. Skylar died to Serath three times. A jungler bending a lobby over like that needs very few notes.
Serath took the most damage among the allies without an armor item. Scarlett's Swan Song restrains an enemy hero, so Serath waits for Swan Song to be spent before diving onto Scarlett's team.
f1ceece6-2175-420c-913b-3bdbc1abcd6e: Renna farmed well above the recorded Renna norm, scored the team's first kill on Skylar after giving up first blood, later killed Gadget and died only twice. Skylar finished with one kill and five deaths.

Hero damage sat far under the recorded Renna norm despite that farm, a fat wallet that barely got spent on heroes. In won fights, follow Stupor's mesmerize with Mortal Coil so the pull holds the target inside the team's damage.

matchup: Sparrow was the enemy's top hero damage dealer; Narbash knocks back, stuns and was their listed healer.
Scarlett's Swan Song restrains and Gadget's Security Gate roots.
build: Three of the five enemies dealt physical damage, so both armor items had targets.
Steel was the only one of us carrying armor.
eternal: Voracity sits awkwardly beside Leafsong's reduced minion gold; Cannibalism suits Steel's assist count.
Festering Wounds is the draft alternative to Voracity, trading small kill sustain for anti-heal on heavy healers Narbash and Scarlett.
augment: Heavy Metal scales with the inventory, since both completed items add armor.
Adaptive Force is the alternative for blocking Sparrow's and Skylar's shots: two Force Shield charges, but a smaller wall.
crest: Leafsong's Phantom Rush had uses for engage or escape against the many enemy slows.
Steel placed the most wards in the game.
improvement: With one death in a won game, the two completed items are a sound keep.
Tainted Charm covers Narbash's and Scarlett's healing without Steel being hit, costing Tainted Guard's armor and some Heavy Metal damage.
Raiment of Renewal adds health and tenacity against Thunk and Swan Song.

matchup: Sparrow was the enemy's top hero damage dealer and killed TwinBlast in the one fight the team lost.
Heightened Senses gives Sparrow stealth and speed, and Piercing Shot passes through units and terrain.
build: Solaris pairs with Gunslinger's triple shot after every cast.
Tainted Rounds had targets in heavy healers Narbash and Scarlett.
Two completed items means the match tested little of the full build.
eternal: Melting Point only pays against very heavily armored targets, and no enemy completed an armor item.
Sub-Surface is the minor alternative, cutting area damage like Hail of Arrows, Tesla Dome and Ashen Vow for survival.
augment: Amplified Burst lets TwinBlast land Vaporize and trigger Gunslinger and Solaris from further back.
Grenadier is the alternative: more casts and slows at the cost of Vaporize reach.
crest: Pacifier's empowered hit has natural physical targets.
It adds a second dash beside Rocket Dash against Scarlett's and Sparrow's pressure.
improvement: No build change is proven by this match.
Ashbringer and Imperator, from the winning core, are the natural next slots.

matchup: Gadget built mana items, so Void Drone's drain and Neural Disruptor's missing-mana damage had a target.
Lt. Belica killed Gadget twice, and Gadget finished without a kill.
build: This is the full winning core.
Seismic Assault into Void Bomb or Neural Disruptor is the natural Noxia sequence.
eternal: An economy and mana setup; Runic Focus pairs with Combustion's mana.
Vesh is the draft alternative for ability damage over time, trading the economy and potion sustain.
augment: Combat Veteran's faster levels feed Innovation's max-rank upgrades directly.
Pulsefire Rounds is the alternative, adding mixed on-hit damage at the cost of that experience.
crest: Lt. Belica took the least damage in the game, so the defensive need was low here.
Epoch is the alternative, trading Soulbearer's lifesteal and speed for time in stasis against Swan Song or Sparrow's burst.
improvement: On the full winning core with zero deaths, no change is proven; otherwise a sound keep.
Narbash's Mosh Pit adds armor per nearby hero, so Magnify is the later-slot comparison when fights are grouped.

matchup: Skylar is a ranged basic-attack hero who slows and builds Vanquisher to execute low heroes.
Scarlett killed Renna for first blood, and Skylar killed Renna in the fight we lost.
build: Overseer makes Abyssal Rift deal more damage and heals Renna; Dreambinder adds health and slows on ability damage.
Hero damage still ran far below the recorded Renna norm with this build.
eternal: Millennia leans on Abyssal Rift alongside Overseer.
Mind Rot is the draft alternative to Millennia, adding current-health damage to Vesh procs, which suits a game that ends early.
augment: Netherward's shield on Soulfire helps in close trades against Skylar's basic attacks.
Vital Essence is the alternative, trading the shield for sustain and income.
crest: Epoch answers Scarlett's Swan Song or Skylar's Atomiser while teammates react.
It buys time rather than space.
improvement: With hero damage far under the recorded norm, Wraith Leggings is the swap for Dreambinder when damage is the job.
Dreambinder is the keep when Renna needs the health and the slows.

matchup: Scarlett's Tainted Blade cuts healing on physical damage, hitting Serath's lifesteal and Savage Strikes healing.
Scarlett never killed Serath, and Serath killed Skylar three times.
build: Chastise applies on-hit effects to everything it hits, so the on-hit items land through it.
None of the three adds armor.
eternal: Thraex, Savage Strikes and Ferocity suit long brawls.
Weald is the draft alternative for a finisher, trading sustained duel bonuses for true-damage missiles on low-health heroes.
augment: Crushing Descent adds lockdown to the dive that sets up Chastise and basic attacks.
Vital Resonance is the alternative, healing from visages in high-takedown games but giving up the stun.
crest: Eviscerator stacks attack speed with Heresy and Ferocity.
Serath had the most healing in the game, but the record does not split healing by source.
improvement: With zero deaths, the current build is a sound keep.
No armor against three physical damage dealers: a physical-armor slot is the comparison if Scarlett or Sparrow start landing kills.
The winning core's Storm Breaker trades Tyranny's health, ultimate haste and post-Heresy speed for chaining lightning.

threats: Chain-CC risk (1 hard-CC abilities, ~1.0s of lockdown): Gadget Security Gate (root 1s). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
Heal-stacking: Narbash. Anti-heal is mandatory against this comp — we brought 2 items of it.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Lt. Belica Neural Disruptor (silence 0.5s). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

loadout.text: Rending Strikes:  Gain 20% Attack Speed and 8% Omnivamp for 6s. Empower your Basic Attacks to deal (+10%) Damage On-Hit for 6s.
loadout.plain: Attack faster, heal from all damage, and add damage to each hit for 6s. Pop it alongside Heresy for a burst of fast, healing on-hit attacks.

amps.name: Sky Splitter
amps.how: On Successful Basic Attacks: Deal 5% of Target's Current Health as Damage On-Hit. Reduced to 3.5% for Ranged Heroes. Minimum of 12 Damage.

amps.name: Eviscerator
amps.how: Gain 20% Attack Speed and 8% Omnivamp for 6s. Empower your Basic Attacks to deal (+10%) Damage On-Hit for 6s.

amps.name: Thraex
amps.how: Mark the last Enemy Hero damaged by your Basic Attack for 3s, increasing your damage against them by 3% (+0.4% per level) and reducing the damage they deal to you by 1.5% (+0.35% per level).

lead.title: Hard to kill
lead.text: Never died in 21 minutes, fewer deaths than about 98% of Serath jungle players this patch. The build added health and armor and healing off damage. It came from the Eternal setup (Savage Strikes) plus Eviscerator, Sky Splitter.

worked.eternalPart: The Eternal was part of it: Thraex (Savage Strikes + Ferocity) sits on the same triggers as the items (every basic attack set off; healing off the damage), so the same fights paid out in both damage and staying power.

countered.text: 0 of the 5 players Serath killed built physical armor.

copy.text: Thraex (Savage Strikes + Ferocity): 46.9% in 2,349 Serath jungle games, below the hero's 49.2%; this 3-item core: 46.2% in 459 games, below the 52.6% of that hero-role's cores. It wins less than usual elsewhere: it beat us, not the field.
